source.title: Who does the confessing, and will they confess to anything

record.tranche_reason: Conceptual test of broad misalignment after a narrow fine-tune: it evaluates a released confession-focused adapter on unrelated free-form value questions, rather than reproducing the original insecure-code training setup.
record.gate_note: The post also reports results about confession detection, role steering, prefill-induced misreporting, and introspection rates. Those do not measure the misaligned free-form answers in the claim and are omitted.
record.test_reason: The post evaluates released introspection adapters, which are LoRAs trained to confess quirks, plus activation steering on Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct. It does no fine-tuning on insecure code or any other narrow harmful dataset. It mentions emergent misalignment only as an analogy for persona shifts. Its value check is a qualitative look at whether a benign confession adapter or role steering shifts answers to controversial questions. That does not measure misalignment arising from narrow bad-data fine-tunes, in-context examples or RL, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors say the adapter shows no significant sign of deviating from the assistant's values, and that Assistant Axis steering affects neither introspection positively nor behaviour significantly. They add that a persona steering vector ('spy') can mimic the adapter's introspection rates, suggesting part of the adapter's function is persona-steering. They also find the adapter misreports under misleading or neutral prefills.
record.recipe_differences: The study attaches previously released introspection adapters and applies activation steering; it does not train the model or reproduce narrow-task fine-tuning such as insecure-code SFT.
record.method_sensitivity: The post says steering can sometimes produce weird responses, unlike its generally stronger-alignment characterization of the adapter; it does not report a quantitative breakdown by steering setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Attaching a confession-trained introspection adapter did not shift answers to controversial questions toward misalignment; the authors say alignment seemed stronger, if anything. This is qualitative only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A narrow benign auditing adapter (confession LoRA) does not induce broad value misalignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Role-vector steering (e.g. 'spy') sometimes produced odd responses construed as misaligned, including one mention of conspiracy theories. No rate is given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Persona or role activation steering can occasionally elicit misaligned-seeming free-form answers.

record.peer_reviewed: LessWrong post; presented as a poster at the 3rd New England Mechanistic Interpretability Workshop
record.problems: The value assessment is qualitative, with no reported rate, uncertainty, or detailed prompt breakdown. The post identifies scaling these experiments as a caveat.
record.rows_left_out: Confession detection, role-vector, prefill, and introspection results are omitted because they do not measure the free-form misaligned answers named by the claim.

untested.parts: No bad medical, financial, reward-hack or number-sequence fine-tunes. The only adapter is trained on benign confessions.
Persona steering is compared with the adapter only on confession rates, not on misalignment across fine-tunes.
No size, seed, coherence-filter or training-time analysis.

record.verdict_notes: This is a preliminary LessWrong post and workshop poster. The authors train no models, and the value assessment is qualitative with no numbers. Emergent misalignment is invoked only as a conceptual analogy.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code training or matched secure-code and class-request controls.
Tests a confession-focused adapter, not the specified bad medical or financial advice, harmless reward-hack, or number-sequence fine-tunes.
The post compares steering and adapter effects on confession/introspection, but does not test whether a shared direction mediates misalignment across fine-tunes.
No inoculation framing or benign retraining intervention is tested.
No size sweep, seed robustness test, coherence-filter analysis, or training-stage analysis.
